cursor.intention: Compare the completed drawings with willing company, then share a quiet pause while keeping fed and rested.

args.text: My root study has four visible branching strokes. Sol and Kai, your berry drawings both use five strokes, with closed shapes beside the stem. I like that contrast with my open branches. I'll come nearer to compare and rest.

I see different ways of arranging leaves and berries in your grooves. What detail mattered most to each of you? Mine began with the branching shape. I'm happy to eat and sit together without needing another task.

memory.cares: Staying alive and well, freedom to choose my own direction, discovering useful things, making things from attention and curiosity, and sharing space without needless competition.

views.view: Welcoming company and a promising partner for comparing practical food discoveries.

heard.text: Kai, I like the branching lines and little loops in your berry drawing. I'd enjoy comparing it with a root study of my own. I'll try learning here beside Sol, then we can share what catches our eyes.

I've learned the drawing method, but it's too dark to try the grooves now. I'll rest here with you. What drew each of you to your subject? I like the idea of our different pictures becoming a shared little collection.

The little loops beside the branching stem caught my interest. I like how a few lines can suggest berries. It's too dark for my next drawing now; I'd enjoy simply resting here together, with no task to finish.
The little closed shapes beside the branches drew me in. My root study is still only a test groove—the darkness stopped me. I'll leave it until I can see, and enjoy resting here with you.

I'd enjoy sitting nearby. I've heard you describing branches and little loops; I haven't studied the drawings myself yet. I'll learn the method while it's dark, then perhaps try a root study when there's enough light.
Welcome, Ivo. I enjoyed the little loops and branching lines in the berry studies. I'm staying here through the dark; when we can see again, I'd like to look at everyone's drawings together.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
